newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti wins Fiat computer deal.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti wins Fiat computer deal.

text.p: Information and technology group Olivetti said on Sunday it had signed a 110 billion lire ($64.4 million) deal to supply Fiat with computers which will link up the Italian carmaker's European sales outlets.
Olivetti's Olsy division, which makes computer systems for companies, will provide both the hardware and software for some 4,000 Fiat showrooms around Europe, an Olivetti spokesman said.
The contract is expected to last between three and four years and might be extended to cover other geographical areas of the Fiat empire.

Fiat and Olivetti, two of Italy's most famous firms which are both based in the northwest, have traditionally had frosty relations, but ties have improved since the resignation last year of Olivetti's long-serving chairman, Carlo De Benedetti.
The deal is a fillip for Olivetti, which is expected to stay in the red in 1997 for the seventh year running.
"It is the first contract of this size we have had with Fiat," Olsy's managing director Claudio Montagner told reporters.
"At the beginning of September we will meet the managing director of Fiat Auto, Roberto Testore, to look into the possibility of consolidating ties, which are now getting better," he added.

Olivetti has not reported a profit since 1990 and sunk to a net loss of 915 billion lire in 1996 after a record 1.60 trillion lire loss in 1995 as it tried to focus on telecoms and information technology.
It sold its personal computer division earlier this year.
